svg.text: Iskar, MSY-001 · midships keel · drawn to scale from the Master Specification, Rev 151
Cut through the forward row of lanes: four cruisers of one battle group in each yard, stacked two high. Keel shutters along the bottom; upper stories simplified.
cruiser spares, stores and refit shops — hatches down into the moorings
Keep and command island above the spine (not drawn)
1,260 m at dock level (hangar wings above: 1,360 m)
2 · PLAN, SEEN FROM BELOW THE KEEL (bow to the left)
Each yard: 2,400 × 400 m, six lanes two abreast in three rows. One battle group at each end; the middle row is split, one lane each.
KEEL SPINE — magazines feed each yard’s gantry through the spine wall
battle group berthed at the forward end (5 cruisers, 3 lanes)
battle group berthed at the after end (5 cruisers, 3 lanes)
Dotted line: gantry run along each yard. Dashed boxes: lane clearance envelope, 750 × 166 m, around a 720 × 156 m cruiser. 4 groups × 5 = 20 Casakins.
Which of a group’s three lanes is the single one is not fixed by the specification; the end rows are drawn stacked here.
3 · LAUNCH, ONE STACKED LANE (side view, simplified)
lower hull descends; partner follows one hull-depth behind
tugs carry both below; drives held until clear
Timings: all four groups clear the keel in ~8 min at action stations · ~3 min for a group already waiting on alert · nearly an hour from routine dock status.
Recovery runs backwards and slower: upper ship first, ~15 min per capture, ~30 min for a battle group.
